info.name: Partner Forum API v1
info.description:
Run in order against the local Development server. Creates fictional test accounts and posts. Passwords are public demo credentials only. All timestamps are UTC; from is inclusive and to exclusive. Page size 1–50. Tags are flagged/unflagged; sort is newest/oldest/likes. Bearer tokens last 30 minutes. Login requests capture token automatically.

Import Local.postman_environment.json and select Forum Local, then run the collection in order. The environment contains baseUrl only; token, newEmail and postId are managed by collection scripts. Saved response examples are synthetic. Datetimes are UTC even where SQL Server serialises a timestamp without a Z suffix. HTTP 400 uses Problem Details/ValidationProblemDetails; unexpected errors use 500 with a traceId. The local API uses HTTP for development only; deployed services require HTTPS. Run scenarios with a fresh seed database where post 1 belongs to Alex.

request.description:
GET is public. Returns {items,total,pageNumber,pageSize}; items contain id, authorId, author, title, body, createdAt, likeCount, commentCount, likedByMe and tags. With a bearer token, likedByMe reflects the current user. Query parameters: page (1–100000, default 1), pageSize (1–50, default 10), author (user ID), from (inclusive UTC date-time), to (exclusive UTC date-time), tag (flagged/unflagged), sort (newest/oldest/likes; default newest). Example: /posts?author=alex&from=2026-09-01T00:00:00Z&to=2026-10-01T00:00:00Z&sort=likes&page=1&pageSize=10. Invalid values or reversed dates return 400. Filters apply to posts. POST requires a bearer token and JSON {title,body}: trimmed title 1–180, body 1–10000 characters. Returns 201 {id} with Location; 400 for validation; 401 if unauthenticated. Author identity always comes from the token.

Saved responses are illustrative schema examples, not credentials or captured user data.

request.description:
GET is public. Query page (default 1) and pageSize (default 10, maximum 50); comments are ordered by creation time then ID. Returns {items,total,pageNumber,pageSize}, with each comment {id,author,body,createdAt}. POST requires Bearer {{token}} and JSON {body} (1–3000 trimmed characters). Returns 201 {id} with Location. Invalid input/page returns 400, anonymous writes 401, missing post 404. Comment endpoints do not support post filters or like sorting.

Saved responses are illustrative schema examples, not credentials or captured user data.

request.description:
Register a regular user. JSON: email (valid address, max 254), password (at least 12 characters, uppercase, lowercase, digit and symbol), displayName (1–80 trimmed characters). Returns 201 with id and displayName; 400 ValidationProblemDetails for invalid/duplicate registration; 429 when throttled. Submitted roles are ignored. Registration does not issue a token; call login next.

Saved responses are illustrative schema examples, not credentials or captured user data.

request.description:
JSON: email and password. Returns 200 with token, expiresAt (UTC), and user {id,name,isModerator}. Invalid credentials or temporary account lockout return 401. Five failed attempts lock an account for five minutes. Auth routes share a per-IP limit of 30 requests/minute and return 429 when exceeded. The script saves the token to the collection variable; do not create an environment variable named token.

Saved responses are illustrative schema examples, not credentials or captured user data.

request.description:
POST requires Bearer {{token}}. No body. Returns 204 (empty body), 401 if anonymous, 404 if post missing, or 409 for an own post or an existing like. The database enforces one like per user/post even for concurrent requests. No unlike operation is exposed.

Saved responses are illustrative schema examples, not credentials or captured user data.

request.description:
POST requires a moderator bearer token. Empty body is supported; optional JSON {label:"Misleading or false information"} accepts only that label. Returns 204, 400 for an unsupported label, 401 if anonymous, 403 for a regular user, 404 if missing, 409 if already flagged. Moderator and timestamp are assigned server-side. Tags remain visible to anonymous readers. No removal operation is exposed.

Saved responses are illustrative schema examples, not credentials or captured user data.
